key_insight: Introducing ConforNets: a latent-space conditioning mechanism integrated into OpenFold3 that enables efficient, controllable sampling of biologically relevant alternate protein conformations, outperforming ad hoc inference-time perturbations.
problem_solved: AlphaFold-style models reliably predict a single dominant fold but fail to recover major alternative conformational states; prior inference-time perturbation methods are inefficient and inconsistent at retrieving functionally important modes.
method: Embed conformational variability into a learned latent space tied to OpenFold3 representations, enabling targeted manipulation of structural modes.
Condition OpenFold3 inference on latent vectors (learned or sampled) to generate diverse, physically plausible conformations without expensive simulation or repeated ad hoc perturbations.
Use supervised/unsupervised latent clustering and targeted sampling to recover major conformational modes and validate against experimental alternate-state structures.
impact: Provides a practical, scalable way for ML practitioners and structural biologists to generate and control multiple protein conformations from a single model, improving downstream tasks like drug design, functional annotation, and multi-state modeling.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: OpenFold3 architecture with a highlighted latent injection point and flow from sequence/MSA → latent control → alternate 3D structures.
Before/after structural comparison: side-by-side ribbon models showing the dominant AF prediction vs. recovered alternate conformations.
Latent-space visualization: 2D projection (t-SNE/UMAP) of latent vectors colored by recovered conformational cluster and annotated with representative structures.
Performance chart: bar/line plot comparing recovery rate, compute cost, and diversity for ConforNets vs. common inference-time perturbation baselines.
paper_title: ConforNets: Latents-Based Conformational Control in OpenFold3
paper_authors: Minji Lee, Colin Kalicki, Minkyu Jeon, Aymen Qabel, Alisia Fadini
